title: Implementation Differences: ppm, IDyOM, and ppidyom
text: blending STM LTM, model gives weight whichever distribution confident — lower entropy means certain predictions. exponent b controls sharply confidence-weighting operates. wi∝(HiHmax)−b,Hmax=log2|alphabet| w_i \propto \left(\frac{H_i}{H_{\max}}\right)^{-b}, \quad H_{\max} = \log_2 |alphabet| b = 1, two models contribute roughly proportion confidence. b = 7 (IDyOM’s default, Pearce 2005), lower-entropy model almost completely dominates — sharp, near-winner-take-blend.

title: Implementation Differences: ppm, IDyOM, and ppidyom
text: Method AX (Moffat 1990) adjusts escape probability using count singleton symbols — symbols seen exactly current context — rather count distinct symbols. intuition symbol seen weak evidence, probability mass escape shorter contexts. Harrison’s ppm ppidyom implement directly: escape = (t₁ + 1) / (C + t₁ + 1) t₁ = count singletons.
code: # R/escape.R — escape_AX esc_numer <- t1 + 1L weight    <- C / (C + esc_numer) escape    <- esc_numer / (C + esc_numer)

title: Implementation Differences: ppm, IDyOM, and ppidyom
text: IDyOM stores AX internally keyword :x. set-ppm-parameters case expression singleton-counting branch type-count keyed :x: IDyOM called :escape :ax (documented keyword), singleton branch never executes — :ax silently produces values :c. correct call :x.
code: ;; ppm-star.lisp — set-ppm-parameters (case escape   (:a  (values 0 1))   (:b  (values -1 1))   ((or :c :x) (values 0 1))   ; ← AX handled as :x internally   (:d  (values -1/2 2))   (otherwise (values 0 1)))   ; ← :ax falls through, accidentally same as :c  ;; ppm-star.lisp — type-count (singleton branch) (:x (let ((count 1))       (maphash (lambda (k v)                  (declare (ignore k))                  (when (= v 1) (incf count 1)))                (transition-counts m location))       count))   ; → 1 + t₁, but only reached when escape = :x, not :ax

title: Compute PPM Probabilities for all symbols with Backoff — ppm_backoff
text: Implements vectorized PPM backoff.  Starting highest order, order assigns probability symbols seen (Ce > 0); probability mass allocated order survives lower orders. Symbols seen order receive remaining mass divided uniform base distribution.

title: Compute PPM Probabilities for all symbols with Backoff — ppm_backoff
text: ## compute_local_probs backoff cascade relate `compute_local_probs` converts raw counts per-symbol local weights: prob_local(s) = max(Ce(s) - subtract, 0) / denom                   denom subtract come escape_func escape_C: denom = C + t, subtract = 0, prob_local(s) = Ce(s)/(C+t). Summing seen symbols: Σ prob_local = C/(C+t) = 1 - esc. backoff cascade (p_mass tracks unallocated probability): p_mass starts 1   n = N downto 0:     seen symbol s (Ce_n > 0):       P(s) = p_mass(s) · prob_local_n(s)   ← allocate share       p_mass(s) *= (1 - prob_local_n(s))   ← reduce remaining share   loop:     unseen symbols: P(s) = p_mass(s) / |alphabet|

text: x Character vector events N Maximum order alphabet Character vector full alphabet order_counts List length N+1 containing count tables orders 0..N. element must `data.table` columns: `index`, `context_id`, `Event`, `Ce`, `C`, `t`, `t1`. - **STM**, `index` corresponds timestep. - **LTM**, `index` constantly -1; `ltm_to_timestep_counts` maps   per-timestep tables loop. escape_func Escape function escape.R (e.g., `escape_C`). Signature: `function(t, t1)` returning `list(subtract, esc_numer)`. Method C standard choice matches ppm package defaults. exclusion Logical. TRUE, applies exclusion (Cleary & Witten 1984). Symbols already seen higher order excluded C computing denom esc lower orders.  Effect: denom shrinks → esc increases → mass flows truly unseen symbols.  Excluded symbols can still receive contrib mass order; denominator changes.

text: ## Math order n, every symbol receives contribution: alpha_n(s) = max(Ce_n(s) - d, 0) / denom_n d = subtract denom_n = context_count + esc_numer, (subtract, esc_numer) returned escape_func (see escape.R): Method : d=0,   eff=1,    ctx=C,       denom=C+1   Method B : d=1,   eff=t,    ctx=C-t,     denom=C   Method C : d=0,   eff=t,    ctx=C,       denom=C+t   Method D : d=0.5, eff=t/2,  ctx=C-0.5t,  denom=C   Method AX: d=0,   eff=t1+1, ctx=C,       denom=C+t1+1 Contributions accumulated across orders using running "remaining mass" (R) shrinks escape probability order: R starts 1   order n:   P(s) += R · contrib_n(s)                   R    *= esc_n   order 0:  P(s) += R · base(s) Expanded (method C concreteness): P(s) =  Ce_N(s)/(C_N+t_N)         + [t_N/(C_N+t_N)] · Ce_N-1(s)/(C_N-1+t_N-1)         + [t_N/(C_N+t_N)] · [t_N-1/(...)] · Ce_N-2(s)/(...)         + ...         + (∏ esc_k) · base(s)
